guest.bio_context: Casey Newton is the editor of Platformer, a technology newsletter, and co-host of the podcast Hard Fork alongside Kevin Roose. He covers artificial intelligence, Silicon Valley, and the tech industry in real time, and has been closely following AI safety issues for several years, including consulting his readers on how to approach AI risk coverage.

pending_qa.q: What is Mark Zuckerberg's vision of 'personal super intelligence' and why does Casey Newton find it dangerous?
pending_qa.r: Zuckerberg's stated goal is to give everyone personal super intelligence to help run their lives, but Newton argues that super intelligence by definition is not personal — if you build something superhuman in every domain, you cannot assume it will listen to you or be aligned with your goals. Newton uses the metaphor of giving everyone a dragon: just because you hand someone a dragon does not mean the dragon will obey them. He argues this framing dangerously underplays the alignment risks of genuinely superhuman AI.
